newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG cuts W.Canada grain, oilseed forecast.
newsitem.headline: UGG cuts W.Canada grain, oilseed forecast.

text.p: United Grain Growers reduced its forecast for western Canadian grain and oilseed production in the 1996/97 (Aug/July) crop year due to cold, wet harvest conditions in the West.
UGG forecast wheat output would total 28.85 million tonnes, down slightly from its earlier projection of 29.09 million but well above Statistics Canada's 1995/96 estimate of 23.85 million.
"Essentially, we've seen this production drop throughout the reports because of this poor harvest weather, the west is worse than the east," UGG analyst Mike Jubinville said.

Wheat quality was better than expected in east Prairies with 87 percent of the hard red spring expected to grade No1 or No2 Canada Western Red Spring in Manitoba, 59 percent in Saskatchewan and 28 percent in Alberta, he said.

Canola production in western Canada this year was projected at 4.87 million tonnes, down from UGG's previous forecast of 4.88 million and sharply below StatsCan's 1995/96 estimate of 6.37 million. Farmers seeded less acres to canola.
Barley production in western Canada was projected at 15.01 million tonnes, down from UGG's previous forecast of 15.56 million, up from StatsCan's 1995/96 estimate of 12.11 million.

"A lot of the barley's still in the field and you're going to have losses as a result. You're going to have spoilage. The stuff that did come off, came off wet and it's going to be heated grain so there's going to be spoilage and production losses," Jubinville said.

Oat production in western Canada this year was projected at 4.34 million tonnes, up from UGG's previous forecast of 4.42 million and sharply higher from StatsCan's 1995/96 estimate of 2.56 million. Farmers seeded more acres to oats this year than in the previous year.
